items.t: Check every university’s terms against its contract
items.when: Before go-live, then whenever a contract is signed or renewed
steps: Open each university on Setup › University terms. “What the contract says” shows the extract and the page or clause.
Check rates by course level, fee basis (net or gross of scholarship), first-year instalments, commission trigger, days to pay, cap, and contract end date.

Set the tier if the university has one: who is counted (all GSP students, per intake, per source country), the bands, and prospective or retrospective. Put universities whose students count together (Kaplan, Study Group) in one group.
Write anything unclear in Open point and ask the account manager in the Institution team.
Set Status to Checked and send for checking. A second person approves it.
items.auto: The engine prices every enrolment from these terms and raises “ready to invoice” on the trigger date.

steps: Put each RP on its scheme (2022 Retrospective, 2024 Tier, flat 70/75/80/85%) or give it its own flat %.
For a non-standard structure, add a copy of the scheme with the RP’s own bands, then point the RP to it.

Record GST registration, payout currency, Australian or local bank account. For an RP under a Master Partner, map it to the Master Partner: GSP pays the Master Partner on the Master Partner’s terms, and the RP’s own terms with the Master Partner stay outside GSP.
RPs without terms: decide whether they get the new-contract default (flat 70%) or wait in exceptions (Settings).
items.auto: Every RP line uses these terms. An RP with no terms is flagged on its first enrolment.

steps: One row per notice, addendum, flyer or email approval that changes what an RP is paid.
Record who it covers (listed RP IDs, or every RP in a region), the enrolment dates, destinations, universities, levels and intakes.
Record the structure: flat %, tier %, % plus a fixed amount, or a milestone lump sum.
Choose how it combines with the RP’s own terms. Usually a separate box: those enrolments do not count toward the RP’s standard tier.
Close the open points in Exceptions › Data gaps (bands cut off in the tracker, missing RP lists).
items.auto: The engine applies a notice to every enrolment that falls in it, on the enrolment date.

items.t: Bring in commission already in progress
steps: For every continuing student, load what the university has already paid and what the RP has already been paid, per instalment.
Load each RP’s count so far in its current tier window, so the next enrolment lands in the right band.
Load open clawbacks and amounts carried forward.
Reconcile the opening balances with Xero before the first payout run.
items.auto: Top-ups and recoveries are worked out from these paid-to-date amounts.

items.t: A university contract is signed, renewed or varied
items.who: Institution team uploads it, Finance enters it
steps: The account manager uploads the signed contract to the university’s record.
Finance edits the university’s terms, sets the new contract end date, and sends for checking.
Use What-if to see how the change moves amounts for current students before approving.
A second Finance person checks it against the contract and approves.
items.auto: Students enrolled before the change keep the terms in force on their enrolment date. Students continue to earn after a contract ends; new enrolments after the end date are held.

items.t: An RP signs, re-signs or changes terms
items.who: RP Ops gets it signed, Finance enters it
steps: RP Ops records the signed agreement.
Finance sets the RP’s scheme or own %, GST status, payout currency, bank account type and payee.
If bank details changed, Finance verifies them; payouts to that RP are held until verified.
A second person approves.
items.auto: New enrolments use the new terms from the date they apply.

items.t: A notice, flyer, addendum or email approval is issued
items.who: Approver or country manager issues it, Finance enters it
items.when: Before the first enrolment it covers
steps: Get the source document and the approver.
Enter the notice: who, when (enrolment dates), where, structure, and how it combines.
Use What-if on the notice to check the effect on current students.
Send for checking. Nothing changes for RPs until it is approved.
items.auto: Milestone bonuses are due once GSP has been paid for the required number of enrolments, even after the notice ends.

steps: Edit the scheme’s bands, counting window or retrospective rule.
Check the effect in What-if.
Send for checking.
items.auto: Every RP on the scheme moves together. Use a separate scheme for one RP’s own bands.

steps: Rates are filled by AI for each currency.
Finance confirms or corrects them.
items.auto: A payout run is held if a currency it needs has no rate for the week.

items.who: Finance: one person prepares, another approves
steps: Open the payout run. It lists every RP line where GSP has received the university’s money, plus top-ups and recoveries.
Clear any hold (missing FX rate) and anything in Exceptions that blocks payment.
Prepare the run. A second person reviews it and approves payment of the invoices the RPs have approved.
Approval creates bills in Xero. Pay batch 1 (Australian accounts) and batch 2 (local accounts).
Preparing the run creates an invoice for each RP on its behalf. The RP approves it, or disputes it with a reason, in the RP portal. Disputed lines stay due and go to the Finance queue.
items.auto: The engine nets recoveries against new commission per RP; a negative balance is carried forward. GST is added for GST-registered RPs and tax is withheld where set.

steps: No terms for an RP or university, a missing rate, or an expired contract: add or fix the terms.
Student type missing: this goes to the application’s admission officer.
Payout run on hold: enter the missing FX rate.
Clawback not recovered in 90 days: forward to Legal.
items.auto: Each exception clears itself once the cause is fixed.

items.when: Once a line is ready to invoice
steps: Lines become “ready to invoice” on their trigger date (census, fees paid, or start + 4 weeks).
Check the student is still enrolled (Admissions confirms enrolment after census).
Approve the invoice in GSP; it is created and sent from Xero (GST at 10% for Australian universities only).
items.auto: The amount, GST and due date come from the university’s terms.

steps: Match each payment in Xero to the student lines it covers.
A lump sum (a university bonus or tier true-up) is recorded on the university, not split per student.
Anything that cannot be matched goes to exceptions.
items.auto: Recording payment makes the RP lines payable and counts the student toward the RP’s tier and any milestone.

steps: For universities that pay annuity (Kaplan colleges, UP Education, AIS), check which continuing students are still enrolled this period. Most universities send a list or a commission statement.
Record withdrawals and leave of absence so later periods stop.
Raise the annuity invoice, or match the university’s statement, then record the payment.
The RP’s share is paid in the next Thursday run.
items.auto: Annuity lines are created for every period of the course and become ready to invoice on their date. Filter the Ledgers by type to see annuity earned and still to come.

steps: Lines past their due date show as “Payment overdue”.
Chase the university; ask the account manager to step in if needed.
items.auto: A task is raised on the due date.

procs.g: When something happens to a student

items.who: Admissions records it, Finance handles the money
steps: Admissions records the withdrawal date and whether there was a refund.
Before a line’s trigger date: nothing is payable. After it, with a refund: the university recovers its commission.
The RP’s share is recovered from its next payouts; the credit stays on the student’s own line.
Not recovered in 90 days: forward to Legal.
items.auto: The engine recalculates every line and the tiers it affects.

steps: Open the student, choose Override on the RP line, enter the amount and confirm.
No reason is needed. The override is logged with the person’s name.
items.auto: The override replaces the calculated amount until it is removed.

steps: Tie university receipts and RP payouts in GSP to Xero.
Investigate differences before the financial month closes.
items.auto: Ledgers in GSP are the source for the reconciliation.

items.when: End of each counting window (calendar year, Apr–Mar, intake)
steps: Check RP top-ups from retrospective tiers are paid in the next run.
Invoice universities for their own tier true-ups and bonuses (for example London Met, UniSC, Federation).
The count resets for the new window.
items.auto: Retrospective top-ups are worked out automatically as each student is paid for.

items.t: Review contracts and notices that are ending
items.who: Finance with the Institution team and country managers
steps: Universities with contracts ending in the next 90 days get a renewal task for their account manager.
Notices ending this month: confirm whether they are extended.
items.auto: New enrolments after a contract ends are held in exceptions.
